questions.question: Systolic pressure is a measure of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ventricular contraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Systolic pressure is the higher number in a blood pressure reading and indicates the pressure in the arteries when the heart's ventricles contract.
 
• It is a critical measure in determining cardiovascular health as it reflects the force exerted on artery walls during heartbeats.
 
• Normal systolic pressure is typically around 120 mm Hg or lower in adults.
 
• Elevated systolic pressure (hypertension) can increase the risk of heart disease and stroke.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Blood Pressure:**

 
 
• Blood pressure is the force of blood pushing against the walls of the arteries as the heart pumps blood.
 
• It is measured in millimeters of mercury (mm Hg) and recorded with two numbers: systolic pressure (higher number) and diastolic pressure (lower number).
 
• Normal blood pressure is usually considered to be 120/80 mm Hg.
 
 
 
• **Diastolic Pressure:**
 
 
• Diastolic pressure is the lower number in a blood pressure reading and indicates the pressure in the arteries when the heart's ventricles are at rest between beats.
 
• Normal diastolic pressure is typically around 80 mm Hg or lower in adults.
 
• Elevated diastolic pressure (hypertension) can also increase the risk of cardiovascular diseases.
 
 
 
• **Ventricular Contraction:**
 
 
• This term refers to the phase of the cardiac cycle when the ventricles contract to pump blood out of the heart.
 
• During this phase, the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the body through the aorta, and the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
 
• Effective ventricular contraction is essential for maintaining adequate blood circulation throughout the body.
 
 
 
• **Hypertension:**
 
 
• Hypertension, or high blood pressure, is a condition in which the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high.
 
• It is often a chronic condition that can lead to serious health issues such as heart disease, stroke, and kidney problems if not managed properly.
 
• Regular monitoring and lifestyle changes, along with medication if necessary, are crucial for managing hypertension.

questions.question: The ratio of the ages of Kamal and Kiran is 4 : 5. After 6 years Kamal's age will be 30 years. What is Kiran's present age?

Kamal's age after 6 years = 30 years

**Calculations:**

4x + 6 = 30.

4x = 30 - 6 = 24

x = 6.

Kiran's present age = 5x = 5 × 6 = 30 years.

**∴ Kiran's present age is 30 years.**

questions.question: Which of the following circulates throughout the body, and stops bleeding by helping to form a blood clot at the site of injury?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Platelets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Platelets, also known as thrombocytes, are small, colorless cell fragments in our blood whose main function is to stick to the lining of blood vessels and help stop or prevent bleeding.
 
• When a blood vessel gets damaged, platelets are activated and gather at the site of injury to form a plug (clot) to stop bleeding.
 
• Platelets are produced in the bone marrow, the spongy tissue inside our bones.
 
• They circulate in the bloodstream for an average of 7-10 days before being removed by the spleen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **White Blood Cells (WBC)**

 
 
• Also known as leukocytes, WBCs are part of the immune system and help the body to fight infections and other diseases.
 
• They are produced in the bone marrow and are found in the blood and lymphatic tissues.
 
• There are several types of white blood cells, including neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, and basophils.
 
 
 
• **Plasma**
 
 
• Plasma is the liquid component of blood, making up about 55% of its total volume.
 
• It is composed mainly of water, but also contains proteins, electrolytes, hormones, and waste products.
 
• Plasma serves as a medium for transporting nutrients, hormones, and proteins to the parts of the body that need it.
 
 
 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBC)**
 
 
• Also known as erythrocytes, RBCs are responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body and returning carbon dioxide from the body to the lungs to be exhaled.
 
• They are produced in the bone marrow and have a lifespan of about 120 days.
 
• RBCs contain hemoglobin, a protein that binds oxygen and gives blood its red color.

• They are home to the planet's highest peaks, including the highest, Mount Everest in Nepal.

• The Himalayas have profoundly shaped the cultures of South Asia; many Himalayan peaks are sacred in Hinduism and Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Shivalik Range**
 
 
• The Shivalik Hills, also known as the Outer Himalayas, extend from the Indus River in the west to the Brahmaputra River in the east.

• It comprises the districts of Almora, Bageshwar, Champawat, Nainital, Pithoragarh, and Udham Singh Nagar.
 
• Kumaon is known for its scenic beauty, rich cultural heritage, and diverse flora and fauna.

questions.question: All the students of a class are sitting in a row facing north. Preeti is 17th from the beginning of the row. Poonam is sitting ahead of Preeti and there are only four students between them. Poonam is 16th from the end of the row. Find the number of students in the class.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

All students are sitting in a row facing north.

Preeti is 17th from the beginning.

Poonam is seated ahead of Preeti, with 4 students in between.

Poonam is 16th from the end.

**Step 1: Position of Poonam from the beginning**

Since Poonam is ahead of Preeti, and there are **4 students between them**, her position from the beginning is: 

Position of Poonam = Position of Preeti − ( 4 + 1 ) = 17 − 5 = 12

**Step 2: Total number of students**

We know that Poonam is **12th from the beginning** and **16th from the end**. Using the formula:

Total students = Position from the beginning + Position from the end − 1

= 12 + 16 − 1 = 27

Thus, the total number of students in the class is **27**. 

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4"**.

questions.question: According to the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, more than 95% of the commercially exploitable wind resources out of the total estimated potential is concentrated in how many states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, more than 95% of the commercially exploitable wind resources in India are concentrated in seven states.
 
• The seven states are Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• These states have favorable geographical conditions such as long coastlines, high wind speeds, and large open spaces which are ideal for wind energy generation.
 
• Wind energy is a crucial part of India's renewable energy strategy and these seven states play a pivotal role in harnessing this resource.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**

 
 
• The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is the nodal Ministry of the Government of India for all matters relating to new and renewable energy.
 
• The broad aim of the Ministry is to develop and deploy new and renewable energy for supplementing the energy requirements of the country.
 
• It focuses on the development of wind energy, solar energy, bioenergy, and other renewable energy sources.
 
• The MNRE also formulates policies, schemes, and programs for the promotion of renewable energy in India.
 
 
 
• **Wind Energy in India**
 
 
• Wind energy is the use of air flow through wind turbines to mechanically power generators for electricity.
 
• India has a total installed wind power capacity of around 38 GW as of 2020, making it the fourth largest wind power producer in the world.
 
• The government aims to achieve a wind power capacity of 60 GW by 2022.
 
• Wind energy is a clean and renewable source of energy that reduces dependence on fossil fuels and helps in reducing greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 
 
• **Commercially Exploitable Wind Resources**
 
 
• Commercially exploitable wind resources refer to the wind energy potential that can be effectively harnessed and converted into electricity using existing technology.
 
• This potential depends on factors such as wind speed, wind direction, and geographical conditions.
 
• Areas with high wind speeds and consistent wind patterns are considered to have high commercially exploitable wind resources.
 
• The seven states mentioned above have been identified as having the highest commercially exploitable wind resources in India.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, which of the following is not a fundamental duty of a citizen?

options.text: Understand the importance of the glorious tradition of our composite culture and preserve it
Men and women have equal right to adequate means of livelihood
Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so
To cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired our national struggle for freedom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Men and women have equal right to adequate means of livelihood**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The statement "Men and women have equal right to adequate means of livelihood" is not listed as a Fundamental Duty in the Constitution of India.
 
• This statement pertains to Directive Principles of State Policy, specifically Article 39(a), which aims to provide equal rights to livelihood.
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution (Article 51A).
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties, which include respecting the Constitution, the National Flag, and the National Anthem; cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle; protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India; promoting harmony; safeguarding public property, and striving for excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
 
 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**
 
 
• These principles are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are not enforceable by any court but are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• Directive Principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life. They also aim to establish social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
 
 
• **Article 39(a)**
 
 
• Article 39(a) of the Indian Constitution directs the State to secure that the citizens, men and women equally, have the right to an adequate means of livelihood.
 
• This is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy and aims to ensure economic justice and reduce inequality in income.

questions.question: Which of these waste items should not be thrown in the general waste?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Old Batteries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Old batteries** contain hazardous materials such as lead, cadmium, and mercury, which can be harmful to the environment and human health.
 
• These hazardous components can leach into the soil and water, causing contamination and posing risks to wildlife and human populations.
 
• Proper disposal of old batteries typically involves recycling or specific disposal methods to prevent environmental damage.
 
• Many regions have designated collection points or recycling centers for old batteries to ensure they are disposed of safely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **General Waste**

 
 
• General waste, also known as residual waste or black bag waste, refers to everyday items that cannot be recycled.
 
• This includes items such as food waste, non-recyclable packaging, and certain household items that do not contain hazardous materials.
 
• General waste is typically collected by municipal waste services and disposed of in landfills or incineration facilities.
 
 
 
• **Recycling**
 
 
• Recycling involves converting waste materials into new products to prevent waste of potentially useful materials.
 
• It helps reduce the consumption of fresh raw materials, energy usage, air and water pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Common recyclable materials include paper, cardboard, glass, aluminum, and certain plastics.
 
 
 
• **Hazardous Waste**
 
 
• Hazardous waste refers to waste that poses substantial or potential threats to public health or the environment.
 
• It includes materials like chemicals, batteries, electronic waste, and certain types of medical waste.
 
• Proper disposal methods for hazardous waste are crucial to prevent environmental contamination and health risks.
 
 
 
• **Electronic Waste (E-Waste)**
 
 
• E-waste refers to discarded electronic appliances such as computers, phones, and televisions.
 
• It often contains hazardous components and valuable materials that can be recycled.
 
• Proper e-waste recycling helps recover valuable materials and prevents environmental pollution.

questions.question: _______ of the Indian Constitution prescribes the qualifications for membership of the Parliament.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 84**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 84 of the Indian Constitution lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament.
 
• A person must be a citizen of India to be qualified for membership of the Parliament.
 
• He/she must be at least 25 years old to be a member of the Lok Sabha (House of the People) and at least 30 years old to be a member of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• Additionally, the person must possess such other qualifications as may be prescribed in that behalf by or under any law made by Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 81**

 
 
• Article 81 deals with the composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• It specifies the maximum number of members in the Lok Sabha and the allocation of seats to the states and union territories.
 
 
 
• **Article 82**
 
 
• Article 82 pertains to the readjustment of seats in the House of the People.
 
• It mandates that upon completion of each census, the allocation of seats to the states and union territories must be readjusted based on the population data.
 
 
 
• **Article 83**
 
 
• Article 83 deals with the duration of the Houses of Parliament.
 
• The Lok Sabha has a term of five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved sooner.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
 
 
• **Article 84**
 
 
• Article 84 lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament, as discussed above.

questions.question:
Find the volume (in cm ³ ) of a solid right circular cylinder whose base diameter is 7 cm and height is 20 cm.

[Use π = 22/7]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Diameter of the base of the cylinder = 7 cm

Radius (r) = Diameter / 2 = 7 / 2 = 3.5 cm

Height (h) = 20 cm

**Calculations:**

Volume (V) of a cylinder is given by the formula:

V = πr²h

Substituting the values:

V = (22/7) × (3.5)² × 20

V = (22/7) × (12.25) × 20

V = (22/7) × 245

V = (22 × 245) / 7

V = 5390 / 7

V = 770 cm³

**∴ The volume of the cylinder is 770 cm³.**

questions.question: Two resistances of 20 Ω each are connected in parallel. This combination is then connected in series with a third resistance of 20 Ω and a 3 V battery. The power supplied by the battery will be _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.30 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The equivalent resistance of two 20 Ω resistors in parallel: R_eq = (20 * 20) / (20 + 20) = 400 / 40 = 10 Ω
 
• The total resistance in the circuit: R_total = 10 Ω + 20 Ω = 30 Ω
 
• The two resistances of 20 Ω each are connected in parallel.
 
• The equivalent resistance of two 20 Ω resistors in parallel is 10 Ω.
 
• This equivalent resistance is then connected in series with a third resistance of 20 Ω.
 
• The total resistance in the circuit is therefore 30 Ω.
 
• The current through the circuit using Ohm's Law:

 I = V / R_total = 3V / 30Ω = 0.1 A
 
• The power supplied by the battery:

 P = V * I = 3V * 0.1A = 0.3 W

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Parallel and Series Resistors:

 
 
• In a parallel circuit, the total or equivalent resistance (R_eq) of resistors can be calculated using the formula:

 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... + 1/Rn
 
• For two resistors R1 and R2 in parallel, the equivalent resistance is given by:

 R_eq = (R1 * R2) / (R1 + R2)
 
• In a series circuit, the total resistance (R_total) is the sum of the individual resistances:

 R_total = R1 + R2 + ... + Rn
 
 
 
• Ohm's Law:
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current (I) through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage (V) across the two points and inversely proportional to the resistance (R) between them:

 I = V / R
 
 
 
• Power Calculation:
 
 
• The power (P) supplied by the battery can be calculated using the formula:

 P = V * I
 
• Using Ohm's Law, we can substitute I = V / R into the power formula to get:

 P = V² / R

questions.question: The exchange of carbon dioxide and oxygen in plants takes place through ______.
questions.solution:

• Diffusion is the process by which molecules move from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.
 
• In plants, diffusion is essential for the exchange of gases such as oxygen and carbon dioxide.

• The process of diffusion does not require energy, making it a passive form of transport in plants.

• This process is not involved in the exchange of gases in plants.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation:**
 
 
• Fermentation is a metabolic process that produces chemical changes in organic substrates through the action of enzymes.
 
• It is used by plants to convert sugars into energy without the use of oxygen.
 
• This process does not play a role in the exchange of gases in plants.
 
 
 
• **Osmosis:**
 
 
• Osmosis is the movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from an area of lower solute concentration to an area of higher solute concentration.
 
• It is a vital process in plant cells for the uptake of water and nutrients.
 
• However, osmosis is not responsible for the exchange of gases like carbon dioxide and oxygen in plants.

• In space, there is a vacuum, meaning there are no particles or atmosphere to scatter light.
 
• The scattering of light is what causes the sky to appear blue when viewed from Earth.

• Photographs of Earth taken from space show a black background due to the absence of atmospheric particles that would scatter light.

• Scattering occurs when light rays encounter small particles in the atmosphere.
 
• The sky appears blue on Earth because molecules in the air scatter blue light from the sun more than they scatter red light.
 
• Rayleigh scattering is the dominant form of scattering in the Earth's atmosphere, which affects shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) more than longer wavelengths (red and orange).
 
 
 
• **Refraction of Light:**
 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another with different densities.
 
• This phenomenon is responsible for various optical effects, such as the bending of a straw in a glass of water.
 
 
 
• **Reflection of Light:**
 
 
• Reflection occurs when light bounces off a surface.
 
• It is the principle behind mirrors and shiny surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Dispersion of Light:**
 
 
• Dispersion is the separation of light into its component colors due to different degrees of refraction for different wavelengths.
 
• This phenomenon is observed in rainbows and prisms.

questions.question: Which of the following aqueous solutions is formed by the reaction of copper sulphate solution with zinc metal?

• A displacement reaction is a type of chemical reaction in which an element reacts with a compound and takes the place of another element in that compound.
 
• In the case of copper sulphate and zinc, zinc displaces copper due to its higher reactivity.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity Series:**
 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• Metals at the top of the series, like zinc, are more reactive and can displace metals below them, like copper, from their compounds.
 
 
 
• **Copper Sulphate (CuSO₄):**

• The soft iron core becomes magnetized when the current flows through the coil, enhancing the magnetic field produced by the coil.

questions.question: A man walking at a speed of 10 km/h crosses a bridge in 7(1)/(2)crosses it in minutes. Find the length of the bridge (in m).

**Given:**

Speed of the man = 10 km/h

Time taken to cross the bridge = 7¹/² minutes = 7.5 minutes

**Calculations:**

Convert time to seconds:

Time in seconds = 7.5 × 60 = 450 seconds

Convert speed to m/s:

Speed in m/s = (10 × 1000) / (60 × 60) = (10000 / 3600) = (50 / 18) m/s

Calculate distance (length of the bridge):

Distance = Speed × Time

Length of the bridge = (50 / 18) m/s × 450 s

Length of the bridge = (50 × 450) / 18

Length of the bridge = 22500 / 18

Length of the bridge = 1250 / 1 = 1250 m

**∴ The length of the bridge is 1250 meters.**

questions.question: A strong magnet is moved towards a stationary coil. When the angle between the direction of motion of the magnet and the plane of the coil is ________, then the induced current in the coil will be minimum.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**90º**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **magnet** is moved towards a stationary coil, an **electromotive force (EMF)** is induced in the coil according to **Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction**.
 
• The magnitude of the induced current depends on the **rate of change of magnetic flux** through the coil.
 
• The **magnetic flux** through the coil is maximum when the motion of the magnet is **perpendicular (90º)** to the plane of the coil.
 
• At this angle, the **rate of change of flux linkage** is zero, which leads to a **minimum induced current** in the coil.
 
• If the magnet moves parallel to the plane of the coil (0º), there is a greater component of the magnetic flux linked to the coil, and the induced current is higher.
 
• Thus, the induced current is **minimum at 90º**, as the alignment of the magnet's motion relative to the coil does not favor significant flux linkage.
 
• This principle is widely applied in **electromagnetic devices**, such as generators and transformers, to optimize current generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction**__

 __
 
• States that an **EMF is induced** in a conductor when the magnetic flux linked with it changes over time.
 
• The induced EMF is directly proportional to the **rate of change of magnetic flux**.
 
• This principle is the basis for the working of devices such as **electric generators, transformers, and induction motors**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Electromagnetic Induction**__
 
 
• Electromagnetic induction is used in **power generation** by hydroelectric, thermal, and wind power plants.
 
• It is applied in **induction heating**, where electrical energy is converted to heat energy for industrial purposes.
 
• Electromagnetic induction finds application in **wireless charging technology** for devices such as smartphones and electric vehicles.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of rainwater harvesting?

options.text: Helping every drop of rain seep into the ground

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The primary purpose of rainwater harvesting is to **capture and store rainwater** for future use, thereby reducing the runoff and wastage of rainwater.
 
• This technique helps in **recharging the groundwater levels** by allowing water to seep into the ground.
 
• Rainwater harvesting can help in **reducing dependence on municipal water supply** by providing an alternative source of water for various uses.
 
• It is an **eco-friendly and sustainable method** to manage and conserve water resources, especially in areas experiencing water scarcity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rainwater Harvesting:**

 
 
• Rainwater harvesting is the process of collecting and storing rainwater for later use. It involves the capture of rainwater from surfaces such as rooftops and other hard surfaces.
 
• The collected water can be used for various purposes including irrigation, gardening, washing, and even drinking after proper treatment.
 
• It is particularly beneficial in areas with irregular rainfall patterns or where the groundwater levels are depleting.
 
• Rainwater harvesting systems can range from simple designs like barrels to more complex systems involving pumps, tanks, and filtration systems.
 
 
 
• **Groundwater Recharge:**
 
 
• Groundwater recharge is the process of water seeping into the ground and replenishing the groundwater levels.
 
• This is a critical process for maintaining the water table and ensuring a sustainable supply of groundwater for various uses.
 
• Rainwater harvesting plays a significant role in enhancing groundwater recharge, especially in urban areas where natural percolation is reduced due to paved surfaces.
 
• Techniques such as recharge pits, trenches, and permeable pavements can be used to facilitate groundwater recharge.
 
 
 
• **Water Conservation:**
 
 
• Water conservation involves the careful use and management of water resources to ensure their sustainability for future generations.
 
• Practices such as rainwater harvesting, efficient irrigation methods, and reducing water wastage are important aspects of water conservation.
 
• Water conservation helps in mitigating the effects of droughts, reducing the burden on water supply systems, and preserving the natural ecosystem.
 
• Public awareness and education on water conservation practices are essential for promoting sustainable water use.
 
 
 
• **Municipal Water Supply:**
 
 
• Municipal water supply refers to the provision of water by local government authorities to urban and rural households and businesses.
 
• This water is typically sourced from rivers, lakes, reservoirs, or groundwater and treated to meet safety standards before distribution.
 
• Dependence on municipal water supply can be high in urban areas, leading to stress on water resources, especially during periods of low rainfall or drought.
 
• Rainwater harvesting can supplement municipal water supply and reduce the pressure on these centralized systems.

__
 
• A precipitate is a solid that forms out of a solution during a chemical reaction.
 
• Precipitates are formed when two soluble substances react and produce an insoluble product.
 
• The solid precipitate can be separated from the liquid components by filtration or decantation.
 
• Precipitation reactions are used in qualitative inorganic analysis to identify the presence of specific ions in a solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Precipitation Reaction**

 
 
• A precipitation reaction occurs when cations and anions in aqueous solution combine to form an insoluble ionic solid called a precipitate.
 
• For example, when solutions of silver nitrate (AgNO₃) and sodium chloride (NaCl) are mixed, the precipitate of silver chloride (AgCl) forms:
 
• AgNO₃(aq) + NaCl(aq) → AgCl(s) + NaNO₃(aq)
 
 
 
• **Filtration**
 
 
• Filtration is a process used to separate solids from liquids or gases using a filter medium that allows only the fluid to pass through.
 
• The solid that remains on the filter is called the residue, and the liquid that passes through is called the filtrate.
 
 
 
• **Decantation**
 
 
• Decantation is a process of separating mixtures by removing a liquid layer that is free of precipitate or sediment.
 
• This technique is used to separate a liquid from insoluble solids or from immiscible liquids with different densities.
 
 
 
• **Qualitative Inorganic Analysis**
 
 
• This is a branch of analytical chemistry that seeks to determine the elemental composition of inorganic compounds.
 
• Qualitative analysis involves identifying the ions present in a sample through specific reactions that produce visible changes, such as precipitate formation.

• It consists of a rotor (the rotating part) and a stator (the stationary part).
 
• When the rotor spins, it induces a flow of electric current within the stator's coils.
 
• This principle is utilized in various applications, including power generation in power plants and portable generators.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Antimony**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Antimony (Sb)** is an element that exhibits properties of both metals and non-metals, categorizing it as a metalloid.
 
• It is found in nature mainly as the sulfide mineral **stibnite (Sb2S3)**.
 
• Antimony has applications in flame-proofing materials, paints, ceramics, and alloys for batteries.
 
• It is used in semiconductors and other electronic devices due to its unique electrical properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metalloids**

 
 
• Metalloids are elements that have properties intermediate between those of metals and non-metals.
 
• They are also known as semimetals.
 
• Commonly recognized metalloids include boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony, and tellurium.
 
• These elements often display semiconductive properties, making them valuable in the electronics industry.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Metalloids**
 
 
• Metalloids typically have a metallic appearance but are brittle and not malleable.
 
• They can form alloys with metals and can also form compounds with non-metals.
 
• They often exhibit intermediate electrical conductivity which can be modified by introducing impurities.
 
• Due to their semiconductive properties, they are crucial in the manufacturing of electronic components such as diodes and transistors.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Antimony**
 
 
• Antimony is used in lead-acid batteries to improve plate strength and corrosion resistance.
 
• It is a component in flame retardants for textiles, plastics, and other materials.
 
• Antimony compounds are used in the production of paints and ceramics.
 
• Its semiconductive properties make it useful in the electronics industry for making diodes and infrared detectors.
 
 
 
• **Other Elements in the Options**
 
 
• **Bismuth:** A metal known for its low toxicity and high density, used in pharmaceuticals and cosmetics.
 
• **Iron:** A metal primarily used in construction and manufacturing due to its strength and abundance.
 
• **Selenium:** A non-metal used in glassmaking and as a dietary supplement due to its antioxidant properties.

__
 
• Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, the ancient texts of Hinduism.
 
• There are two primary branches (Shakhas) of Yajurveda: Shukla (White) Yajurveda and Krishna (Black) Yajurveda.
 
• Shukla Yajurveda is also known as Vajasaneyi Samhita, and it is further divided into Madhyandina and Kanva Shakhas.
 
• Krishna Yajurveda contains mixed prose and verses and is further divided into Taittiriya, Maitrayani, Kathaka, and Kapisthala-Katha Samhitas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yajurveda**

 
 
• Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, which also include Rigveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• The Yajurveda is primarily a compilation of ritual offering formulas that were said by a priest while an individual performed ritual actions such as those before the yajna fire.
 
• It is divided into two major recensions known as the "black" (Krishna) and the "white" (Shukla) Yajurveda.
 
• Shukla Yajurveda, or White Yajurveda, contains only the mantras, while Krishna Yajurveda, or Black Yajurveda, has a mixture of prose and verses.
 
 
 
• **Shukla Yajurveda**
 
 
• Also known as Vajasaneyi Samhita.
 
• It is divided into Madhyandina and Kanva Shakhas.
 
• Each of these branches has its own unique set of mantras and verses.
 
 
 
• **Krishna Yajurveda**
 
 
• Contains a mixture of prose and verses.
 
• It is further divided into Taittiriya Samhita, Maitrayani Samhita, Kathaka Samhita, and Kapisthala-Katha Samhita.
 
• Each of these Samhitas has its own unique characteristics and content.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Yajurveda**
 
 
• Yajurveda plays a crucial role in Vedic rituals and ceremonies.
 
• It is used by the Adhvaryu priest, who is responsible for the physical details of the rituals, including the measurements and construction of the altar and other ritual implements.
 
• The mantras of Yajurveda are recited in conjunction with the performances of various sacrificial rites.

questions.question: Find the least common multiple (LCM) of 70, 28 and 42.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers = 70, 28, and 42

**Calculations:**

**Step 1: Prime Factorization**

⇒ 70 = 2 × 5 × 7

⇒ 28 = 2² × 7

⇒ 42 = 2 × 3 × 7

**Step 2: Identify the Highest Powers**

⇒ For 2: Highest power is 2² (from 28)

⇒ For 3: Highest power is 3¹ (from 42)

⇒ For 5: Highest power is 5¹ (from 70)

⇒ For 7: Highest power is 7¹ (common in all)

**Step 3: Calculate the LCM**

LCM = 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ × 7¹

LCM = 4 × 3 × 5 × 7

Calculating:

⇒ 4 × 3 = 12

⇒12 × 5 = 60

⇒ 60 × 7 = 420

**∴ The least common multiple (LCM) of 70, 28, and 42 is 420.**

questions.question: Select the correct example for mechanical barrier method of contraception from the options given below.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Condoms** are a mechanical barrier method of contraception.
 
• They are designed to prevent sperm from entering the uterus and thus prevent fertilization.
 
• Condoms are available for both males and females, though male condoms are more commonly used.
 
• This method is not only effective in preventing pregnancy but also in protecting against sexually transmitted infections (STIs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Also known as a vasectomy, it is a permanent method of contraception for men.
 
• It involves cutting or sealing the vas deferens, which are the tubes that carry sperm from the testicles to the urethra.
 
• While effective, it is not considered a mechanical barrier method.
 
 
 
• **Use of Copper-T**
 
 
• It is an intrauterine device (IUD) that is inserted into the uterus to prevent pregnancy.
 
• The copper ions released by the device are toxic to sperm and egg, preventing fertilization.
 
• This method is a form of long-term contraception but not a mechanical barrier method.
 
 
 
• **Use of Birth Control Pills**
 
 
• These are hormonal contraceptives taken orally by women.
 
• They work by preventing ovulation, thickening cervical mucus, and thinning the uterine lining.
 
• While effective, they are not considered a mechanical barrier method.

questions.question: What happens when calcium sulphate hemihydrate is mixed with water?

options.text: It solidifies as a hard solid mass.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It solidifies as a hard solid mass.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When calcium sulphate hemihydrate (commonly known as plaster of Paris) is mixed with water, it undergoes a chemical reaction.
 
• The chemical reaction results in the formation of calcium sulphate dihydrate (gypsum).
 
• This reaction causes the mixture to solidify and form a hard, solid mass.
 
• The process is exothermic, meaning it releases heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate (Plaster of Paris)**

 
 
• Calcium sulphate hemihydrate is obtained by heating gypsum (calcium sulphate dihydrate) to about 150°C.
 
• It is widely used in construction, medical applications (such as casts), and artistic sculptures.
 
• The chemical formula for calcium sulphate hemihydrate is CaSO₄·0.5H₂O.
 
 
 
• **Gypsum (Calcium Sulphate Dihydrate)**
 
 
• Gypsum is a naturally occurring mineral and is composed of calcium sulphate dihydrate (CaSO₄·2H₂O).
 
• It is commonly used in the manufacture of drywall, plaster, and fertilizers.
 
• Gypsum has the ability to absorb and release moisture, making it useful in regulating humidity levels.
 
 
 
• **Exothermic Reaction**
 
 
• An exothermic reaction is a chemical reaction that releases energy in the form of heat.
 
• This type of reaction often results in an increase in temperature of the surrounding environment.
 
• In the case of mixing plaster of Paris with water, the heat released helps to speed up the setting process.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Plaster of Paris**
 
 
• Plaster of Paris is used in the medical field to create casts for broken bones because it hardens quickly and holds the bone in place.
 
• It is also used by artists for making sculptures and decorative objects.
 
• In construction, it is used for creating false ceilings, wall decorations, and other architectural elements.

Expression = x² + y² + (x − y)² + (x + y)² - 20

**Calculations:**

**Step 1: Expand the Squares**

 
• (x − y)² = x² - 2xy + y²
 
• (x + y)² = x² + 2xy + y²

**Step 2: Substitute the Expanded Forms**

x² + y² + (x² - 2xy + y²) + (x² + 2xy + y²) - 20

**Step 3: Combine Like Terms**

3x² + 3y² - 20

**Step 4: Factor Out Common Terms**

3(x² + y²) - 20

**∴ The simplified expression is 3x² + 3y² - 20.**

questions.question: When a ray of light enters from a denser medium to a rarer medium, then _______.

options.text: It bends away from the normal.
Its angles of incidence and refraction are equal.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It bends away from the normal.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a ray of light enters from a **denser medium** (e.g., water) to a **rarer medium** (e.g., air), it bends **away from the normal** due to the change in the speed of light.
 
• This phenomenon is governed by the principle of **refraction.**
 
• The bending of light occurs because light travels **faster in a rarer medium** and slower in a denser medium.
 
• The degree of bending depends on the **refractive index** of the two media. The refractive index measures how much light slows down in a medium compared to the vacuum.
 
• Refraction follows **Snell's Law**, which is expressed as: *n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂*, where **n₁** and **n₂** are the refractive indices of the two media, and **θ₁** and **θ₂** are the angles of incidence and refraction respectively.
 
• In this case, the refractive index of the denser medium is higher, so the light ray bends **away from the normal** when it enters the rarer medium.
 
• This concept is widely applied in technologies like **lenses, prisms, and optical instruments**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: It is not refracted**__

 __
 
• Light is always refracted when it passes between two media with different **refractive indices**, unless it hits the boundary at a **normal incidence** (i.e., at 90° to the surface). This option is incorrect because refraction is a natural phenomenon that occurs during such transitions.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: It bends towards the normal**__
 __
 
• Light bends **towards the normal** only when it passes from a **rarer medium** into a **denser medium**, such as from air to water. This option does not apply to the given scenario where light moves from a denser to a rarer medium.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Its angles of incidence and refraction are equal**__
 
 
• Angles of incidence and refraction are equal only when the refractive indices of both media are the same, or when light passes perpendicular to the surface. This option is incorrect as the media have different **refractive indices.**

questions.question: A beam of light parallel to the ________ of a concave mirror will pass through the principal focus after reflection.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Main axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A concave mirror is a mirror with a reflecting surface that curves inward.
 
• The main axis, or principal axis, is an imaginary line that passes through the center of curvature and the vertex of the mirror.
 
• When a beam of light parallel to the principal axis strikes a concave mirror, it reflects and converges at the principal focus.
 
• The principal focus is the point where parallel rays of light either converge (concave mirror) or appear to diverge from (convex mirror) after reflecting from the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror has a reflective surface that is curved inward, resembling a portion of the interior of a sphere.
 
• It is used to focus light and form real, inverted images when the object is placed beyond the focal length.
 
• Concave mirrors are commonly used in telescopes, headlamps, and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Principal Focus:**
 
 
• The principal focus of a concave mirror is the point on the principal axis where light rays parallel to the principal axis converge after reflection.
 
• The distance between the mirror's surface and the principal focus is called the focal length.
 
 
 
• **Reflection of Light:**
 
 
• Reflection is the change in direction of a wavefront at an interface between two different media so that the wavefront returns into the original medium.
 
• Concave mirrors reflect light inward to one focal point, which is why they are used to focus light.
 
 
 
• **Main Axis (Principal Axis):**
 
 
• The principal axis is an imaginary line that passes through the center of curvature and the vertex of the mirror.
 
• It is important in understanding the path of light rays in concave and convex mirrors.

• The state celebrates numerous festivals like Diwali, Holi, Teej, and Gangaur with traditional fervor.

• Rajasthani languages include Marwari, Mewari, Dhundhari, Harauti, and others.
 
• These languages are part of the Indo-Aryan language family.
 
• Despite the prevalence of Rajasthani dialects, Hindi serves as the official language for administrative purposes.
 
• The use of Hindi in education and government ensures uniformity and accessibility across the state.
